newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to rely more on foreign funds for projects.
newsitem.headline: Manila to rely more on foreign funds for projects.

text.p: The Philippines is scaling down its funding allocation for infrastructure projects for next year and will turn more to foreign lenders to finance some of them, the budget department said.

Data released by the department on Saturday show government allocation for locally funded projects, in transporation and communication sectors, would drop by 27 percent to 51.8 billion pesos in 1977 from 71.2 billion pesos earmarked for this year.
Foreign-assisted projects, in turn, will increase to 35.5 billion pesos next year from 27.1 billion pesos this year, the data showed.

Budget department officials said the government would need to turn to foreign lenders to finance some projects because the bulk of its operating expenses would be used to cover increases in civil servants' pay and higher allotments for local governments.
Among foreign creditors it was expected to rely on are the Japan international Cooperation Agency (JICA), the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank, they said.
